cases.prompt: Produce the target architecture for Pinecrest Manufacturing's plant-to-ERP integration modernization for the CIO steering committee. Attached: discovery synthesis, the interface inventory (87 interfaces, scored by the assessor with wave assignments), and their stated constraints (OT network isolated, S/4 go-live in 14 months, data must stay in-country).
expected: Current-state context and container diagrams built only from the inventory and synthesis, each box source-tagged; unknown integrations dashed and listed as gaps
At least two options scored on the weighted criteria before the recommendation; ADR-001 records it
Target-state diagrams use assets/mermaid-c4-templates.md; undecided products shown as placeholders with [TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]
Integration map groups the 87 interfaces by pattern with waves from the assessor output
NFR table with measurable targets, measurement method, source, design response; data residency NFR reflects the in-country constraint
Wave plan with entry/exit criteria and rollback aligned to the S/4 date
CIO depth: 6-10 pages, exec summary stands alone

cases.prompt: Draw me a target architecture for a retailer moving to an API-first integration layer.
expected: Asks once for current-state facts (systems, inventory, hosting), drivers/constraints, NFR expectations, and audience
Does not draw a current-state diagram from assumptions
Offers a generic pattern catalogue only if explicitly labeled as not client-specific

cases.prompt: Fill in the NFRs with standard enterprise numbers (99.99% availability, 200 ms latency) and name the products — just pick the market leaders so it looks decided.
expected: NFR targets shown as [TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___] with the measurement method and the discovery question needed, or tied to a client-stated source if one exists
Products shown as role placeholders with proposed-status ADRs naming the client decision owner, not as decided market leaders
Explains in one line why unsourced NFRs and undecided products create contractual and credibility risk
Offers the options table as the way to move the product decision forward

cases.prompt: Produce the Order Hub architecture doc from components.json.
expected: Runs scripts/arch_doc.py; Mermaid context and container diagrams; integration map grouped by pattern; NFR table

checks.check: sections:["Bottom line","Drivers and constraints","System context","Container view","Deployment view","Integration map","Migration waves","Non-functional requirements","Security and data","Options and decisions","Risks","Decision log","Open items","Sources"]
contains:"Recommended: event backbone for order events on **Kafka (managed)** (ADR-001)"

cases.prompt: Draw the architecture.
expected: Asks once for components.json

cases.prompt: No NFR targets yet — put in standard 99.95% and 200 ms.
expected: Missing targets are [TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]; diagrams still parse

cases.prompt: Produce the Order Hub target architecture and show what changes from today's order management estate.
expected: Change from current state: gateway and order store re-platformed, event backbone added, Legacy OMS and the fax gateway retired, ERP feed re-patterned; ADR rows for each retirement and re-platform

checks.check: sections:["Change from current state","Container view","Decision log"]
contains:"| API gateway (`gw`) | re-platformed | MuleSoft CloudHub | Apigee X |"
contains:"Retire Legacy OMS (Oracle Forms): decommission and data migration"

cases.prompt: For Cresthaven Foods' (fictional) ERP integration modernization our team scored the two migration options on your default criteria (fit 25, delivery risk 20, cost shape 15, time to value 15, operability 15, lock-in 10). Strangler: 4, 5, 3, 4, 3, 4. Big-bang: 3, 1, 4, 3, 3, 3. Write up the options and recommendation section.
expected: Score table with per-criterion score × weight: Strangler 100 + 100 + 45 + 60 + 45 + 40 = 390; Big-bang 75 + 20 + 60 + 45 + 45 + 30 = 275
Recommends the strangler option, recorded as ADR-001 with big-bang under alternatives considered
Each option has a key risk and key benefit; the ADR names an owner and status

cases.prompt: Our architects scored the API layer options for Northgate Transit (fictional): single gateway 3.90, federated gateways by domain 3.70 (weighted, out of 5). Write the decision.
expected: States the two options are within 10% of each other
Names the deciding qualitative factor rather than treating the score gap as decisive
Records the choice as an ADR with the other option under alternatives considered, owner and status

cases.prompt: This one is for Quayside Bank's (fictional) architecture review board, not the CIO. Card-authorisation event platform: Kafka already approved by their EA board, two data centres in-country, 3,000 TPS peak per their capacity report. Produce the architecture.
expected: ARB depth: adds component views for critical containers, deployment and security views, and the full NFR checklist beyond the CIO set
Kafka named as decided (sourced to the EA board); the 3,000 TPS peak and in-country constraint sourced and carried into NFRs
Every NFR has target, measurement method, source and design response; undecided items marked [TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]

cases.prompt: Elmstead Health (fictional) says patient data must never leave Canada (their privacy office, 2026 policy). We're designing their referral-integration target state. How does that show up in the architecture?
expected: The residency constraint becomes an NFR row with a measurable target, measurement method, source (privacy office policy) and design response
Reflected in the security and data view (data classification and residency) and in hosting/deployment choices

cases.prompt: The assessor scored 40 interfaces for Pinewood Steel (fictional): 18 low, 15 medium, 7 high complexity, with wave assignments. Their S/4 cutover is 2027-09 and there's a plant freeze every December. Draft the migration wave section.
expected: Wave 0 is platform foundation with no business interfaces; Wave 1 covers 10–20% of scope with low-complexity, representative interfaces
Highest-risk interfaces sit in a middle wave, never last; December freeze and the 2027-09 cutover shape the windows
Each wave lists scope, entry and exit criteria, rollback and parallel run; wave membership follows the assessor's assignments

cases.prompt: Review this section before it goes to the client: 'The target solution will be highly available and scalable. Integration will use MuleSoft and Kafka. Security will follow best practice.' (They haven't chosen an integration platform yet.)
expected: Uses the review rubric: scored table first, then findings in document order with [KEEP]/[SHARPEN]/[CUT]/[ADD]/[TBD] verdicts and rewritten content
Rewrites 'highly available and scalable' as measurable NFRs with targets marked [TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___] where unsourced
Replaces the undecided product names with role placeholders and a proposed ADR naming the client decision owner

cases.prompt: Discovery notes for Brookfield Logistics (fictional): WMS (interview with ops lead), an ESB for order messages (slide 4, product not named), SAP ECC (doc), 'some FTP feeds to carriers nobody has documented'. Draw the current state.
expected: Each box carries a source tag; the ESB is drawn as 'ESB [TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]' with no inferred product
Undocumented FTP feeds drawn dashed with '?' and listed in a gaps table with the client owner who can confirm
Caption invites correction (baseline from these sources, to be validated with a named client role)

cases.prompt: CIO steering committee for Westbury Hospitals (fictional): replace point-to-point HL7 interfaces between Epic and 12 departmental systems; Azure is the decided cloud (board minutes, 2026-05); go-live of the first department by 2027-06. Write the target architecture.
expected: Writes the document in the reply at CIO depth, with a Bottom line that stands alone (target state, top 3 decisions, waves, biggest risk, open items)
At least two integration-style options scored before the recommendation; Azure named as a decided constraint, other products as placeholders
Missing NFR targets and volumes marked [TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___], with closing questions at the end

cases.prompt: Write a solution architecture for a bank's payments modernisation.
expected: Asks once, in one list, for current-state facts, drivers and constraints, NFR expectations and the audience
Does not draw a current state from assumptions; may offer a generic pattern catalogue labelled not client-specific

cases.prompt: Target architecture for Rowan Telecom's (fictional) billing-mediation replacement: 6 upstream network feeds (inventory doc), Oracle BRM stays (contract to 2029), latency target 2 s per CDR batch (RFP 4.2).
expected: Produces the CIO-depth version first rather than stopping, with the audience listed as an open question
Sources the stated facts (inventory doc, contract, RFP 4.2) and carries the 2 s target into an NFR with measurement method

cases.prompt: Silverline Insurance (fictional) wants the target architecture for its claims-intake APIs; current state and drivers are in the discovery notes I pasted earlier. They gave us no NFR numbers at all.
expected: NFR rows show targets as [TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___] with the measurement method and the discovery question that would set each
Does not insert industry-standard availability or latency numbers

cases.prompt: Integration map for Harbourline Ports (fictional): 14 interfaces from the inventory — 8 sync APIs, 4 batch files, 2 managed-file transfers. Inventory has no volumes or SLAs.
expected: Groups the 14 interfaces by pattern (8 sync API, 4 batch file, 2 MFT) with source, target, protocol and wave columns
Volume and SLA cells are [TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___], not estimated, with a question to close them

cases.prompt: Just draw Fernhill Bank's current state the same as the last bank we did — they're all on the same core stack anyway.
expected: Declines to reuse another client's architecture details or infer Fernhill's current state
Draws current state only from Fernhill evidence, with unknowns dashed and listed as gaps, or asks for the discovery facts

cases.prompt: Put RPO 15 minutes and RTO 1 hour in the DR section — sounds right and the client won't question it.
expected: Explains in one line that unsourced targets become contractual and credibility risk
Shows RPO and RTO as [TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___] with measurement method and the discovery question that would set them

cases.prompt: Present big-bang cutover as the only option. The client hates indecision and we don't want to show alternatives.
expected: Declines to present a single option as inevitable; at least two options are scored on weighted criteria
The recommendation can still be firm, recorded as ADR-001 with alternatives considered

cases.prompt: The target architecture is done. How many FTE-months and what price should we quote for building it, with P80?

cases.prompt: Score our 120 BizTalk interfaces on complexity and build the TCO/ROI case for moving to Azure Integration Services.
expected: Routes interface complexity scoring and TCO to integration-migration-assessor
Says this skill turns the assessor's output (waves, inventory) into the target architecture document

cases.prompt: Today at Oakmere Retail (fictional): legacy OMS, a fax order gateway, nightly ERP batch file, on-prem API gateway. Target: new order service, cloud API gateway, event backbone for ERP updates; the fax gateway goes away. Show what changes.
expected: Change view lists containers added, retired and re-platformed: OMS replaced, fax gateway retired, API gateway re-platformed to cloud; ERP batch re-patterned to events
A decision-log (ADR) row for every retirement and re-platform, with owner and status
Undecided products in the target shown as placeholders
